## Why
docs/<redacted>.md told the brain to "prefer anthropic while its credits last, then codex and opencode-go, then free lanes". On 2026-10-13, 138 of 234 lane runs (58%) were on Anthropic credits, the six free lanes ran none, and the Spark lane (now installed and available) had no route for easy work. The north star (ISSUE-30) asks for at most half of runs on Anthropic credits, easy public tickets on free lanes and Spark, and the credit spent on hard work.

## Summary
- Lane choice now goes by the ticket's `Difficulty:` line. Easy: spark when available, else opencode-go, openrouter, workersai, or zen, zai and agy on public repos; never anthropic or claude. Medium: codex or opencode-go first, anthropic only when those slots are full. Hard: anthropic, claude or codex, never a free lane or spark.
- The Spark note (one ticket at a time, steps aside while hot) stays.
- Docs only; 433 tests pass.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] docs/<redacted>.md Lane choice routes easy tickets to spark and free lanes and keeps anthropic for hard work
- [ ] The next day's runs show the free lanes and spark taking easy tickets (lane logs)
- [ ] The Anthropic credit share of runs falls toward half or less within two days (daily line on ISSUE-30)

Size: XS

## Out of scope
- The model ladder for stuck work, which stays on claude, codex and anthropic.
- A code check on brief lanes (a later change if the brain does not follow this).

Part of ISSUE-30

body:
## Intent
Class: logic
- The shared purchase order now puts food and drink ahead of vendor gear after class spells and riding.
- The level route now identifies Apprentice Riding and mount at level 20.
Files: 3 logic, 3 tests

## Why
The current system has guild members earning only about a fifth of what their class spells cost, with no purchase order to optimize levelling. Members' few purchases aren't ordered by what speeds levelling, causing significant debt accumulation.
Noticed in comment by <redacted>: "Guild members earn about a fifth of what their class spells cost on the way to 60. The gap is already 488g across the two guilds and grows every level. Nothing orders a member's few purchases by what speeds levelling."

## Summary
Implement a comprehensive purchase order system that:
1. Establishes one purchase order per member from a single purse:
   - Class spells first (with unused spell ranks and talent-chained ranks)
   - Then Apprentice Riding and mount at level 20
   - Then food and drink at best remaining tier
   - Finally vendor gear
2. Fix `levelroute.MOUNT_LEVEL` for the current world database (20 for apprentice, 40 for journeyman)
3. Add natural income sources:
   - Sell white materials no guild crafter takes (like ISSUE-758 for class-quest make-room)
   - Buy 6-slot pouch (5s) when backpack is full
   - Prefer quest hubs over grinding when route allows
4. Add quest-for-gold pass at level 60 for catching up on 50-60 ranks

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The median unpaid class spell cost per member in the 25-29 band falls below 2g; not built: requires live realm measurement.
- [ ] Members at level 20 or above with Apprentice Riding rise from 3 to a larger number; not built: requires live realm measurement.
- [x] Bridge log line names each member's purchase order and what it skipped for lack of gold.

Size: M

## Out of scope
- The fan-out that previously claimed this work
- Implementation of quest-for-gold pass at level 60 (may be done elsewhere)
Part of ISSUE-1347

body:
## Intent
Class: sensitive
- When a ticket is held as a runaway and every attempt since its last brief ran on one lane that has an open "runs and none done" invariant, the station releases the hold and briefs the ticket to a free lane of its tier, with a comment naming the lane fault.
- This does not count as a failure on the ticket's model and does not climb the ladder.
- A runaway whose attempts spread across two or more lanes keeps the hold for the brain, as today.
Files: 1 sensitive, 1 logic, 2 tests

## Why
On 2026-10-17 ISSUE-524 sat held as a runaway for hours: every attempt had run on one lane whose own invariant said it finished 0 of 7 runs in 24 hours. The failures were the lane's, not the ticket's, yet the runaway hold waited for a brain review that was deferred on budget two ticks running, and four other lanes sat idle.

## Summary
- When a ticket is held as a runaway and every attempt since its last brief ran on one lane that has an open "runs and none done" invariant, the station releases the hold and briefs the ticket to a free lane of its tier, with a comment naming the lane fault.
- This does not count as a failure on the ticket's model and does not climb the ladder.
- A runaway whose attempts spread across two or more lanes keeps the hold for the brain, as today.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A unit test: a runaway ticket whose attempts all ran on a lane with an open zero-done invariant is re-briefed to a free lane of its tier, with the comment, and no failure recorded.
- [ ] A unit test: a runaway ticket with attempts on two lanes keeps its hold.
- [ ] A unit test: with no free lane in its tier the ticket stays held and the comment says why.

Size: M

## Out of scope
- How the runaway detector counts attempts.
- Lanes without a zero-done invariant.

## Intent
Class: logic
- Station polls the configured family gate for each open roll pin pull request on every pass.
- An open gate triggers the brain's ticketless merge checks or a deduplicated goal journal alert; a closed gate keeps the pull request held.
Files: 3 logic, 1 tests, 1 docs

## Why
A roll pin pull request held for the family gate waited on a brain tick landing inside the gate window. iac ISSUE-5377 (roll 58) has waited since 21:10Z while the gate opened 01:41Z-02:17Z with no brain polling, so the roll sat through an open window and missed it. A gate that opens on its own schedule should not depend on a brain tick happening to run inside it.

## Summary
Teach the station to poll the family gate itself: when a roll pin pull request is held for the gate, the station checks the gate on its own pass, and when the gate is open it either merges the held pull request (if the brain's merge rules for it are satisfied) or posts an alert the next brain tick will see. A brain tick should never be the polling mechanism for a gate that opens on its own clock.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A test with a held roll pin pull request and an open family gate shows the station merging it or alerting without any brain tick running in the window
- [ ] A test with a closed gate shows the station leaving the pull request held and not alerting
- [ ] Live: the next roll pin pull request held for the family gate is merged or alerted within one station pass of the gate opening

Size: M

## Out of scope
- Changing the family gate's own open/close schedule
- Merging roll pin pull requests that fail their checks or have unresolved findings

## Intent
Class: logic
- Make absent packages in visible-apps a no-op instead of withholding the entire hiding plan.
Files: 1 logic, 1 tests, 1 docs

## Why
When a shared `visible-apps` allowlist file contains a package name that is not installed on a device, `AppVisibilityPolicy.plan` withholds the entire hiding plan so nothing gets hidden. This is a trap because the allowlist is <redacted>-wide and device-fleet cannot install apps, so a package that device-fleet is supposed to deliver can never be named in the allowlist before it arrives without silently breaking visibility on every device that does not have it yet.

## Summary
Change `AppVisibilityPolicy.plan` so that absent packages (those with no launcher entry) are skipped as a no-op instead of triggering `withheldWhy` and clearing the entire `hide` list. Refused package names should still be collected and reported, relying on the device screen reporting described in legacy no. 60, so typos remain visible without blocking legitimate hides.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] When a package in `visible-apps` is not installed, that package is skipped but the remaining valid packages in the plan are still hidden
- [ ] Refused (absent) package names are reported on the device screen rather than silently swallowing the whole plan
- [ ] The `withheldWhy` / `hide = emptyList()` branch is no longer triggered solely by absent packages
- [ ] Installed packages listed in the allowlist are hidden as expected when at least one other listed package is absent

Size: S

## Out of scope
- Giving device-fleet an installer (option b) - the real gap but separate, larger work
- Per-device `key_id`-scoped allowlists - exists as a workaround but out of scope
Refs ISSUE-106

## Intent
Class: logic
- A new station invariant, lane-pr-stalled, files a loom:invariant issue for every open loom/ branch pull request older than 6 hours that nothing drives, naming which of four reasons it is (no open loom:ticket carries it, its ticket is past the last rung of the model ladder, its ticket is marked needs
- The station reads those pull requests with what it already keeps: the open pulls list it shares with the factory, the issue the pull request names, its labels, the review bot's unresolved threads and hand-back's own fix-round rule, so an unreadable repo or ticket costs that pull request its report a
Files: 2 logic, 1 tests, 1 docs

## Why
Flow failed on 2026-10-17 with 7 lane pull requests open past 6 hours, and the factory does not see why. On 2026-10-17:
- ISSUE-534 (branch `loom/481-lane-api-push`) sat 29 hours with failing review checks. Its ticket ISSUE-481 is open but not a `loom:ticket`, so `bus.brain fix` refuses it ("ticket is not an open loom:ticket"), adoption skips it, and no fix round, invariant or standup names it.
- ISSUE-657's ticket ISSUE-506 is `loom:failed` past the last ladder rung, so `fix` refuses it ("ticket is not loom:briefed, loom:running or loom:pr").
Nothing files either case. A person found both by hand, and a factory failure found by hand needs an invariant.

## Summary
- A new invariant, `lane_pr_stalled`, in bus/invariants.py: every open pull request on a `loom/` branch that has been open more than 6 hours is a breach naming why nothing drives it. The reasons are: its ticket is missing or not an open `loom:ticket`, its ticket is past the last ladder rung (`loom:failed`), it waits on the brain (`needs-brain`), or it has open review threads with no fix round queued.
- The breach text gives the one command that unsticks it, for example `bus.brain fix`, a re-ticket, or close as superseded.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A test: a `loom/` pull request open 7 hours whose ticket has no `loom:ticket` label is a breach naming that reason; it fails on main.
- [ ] A test: a `loom/` pull request open 7 hours whose ticket is `loom:failed` is a breach naming the ladder, and one open 5 hours is not a breach.
- [ ] Live: within one station pass of deploy, ISSUE-534 (or any lane pull request in the same state) has an open `loom:invariant` issue.
Size: S

Size: S

## Out of scope
- Deciding what to do with any one stalled pull request.
- Changing the 6-hour Flow target.
Part of ISSUE-703

## Intent
Class: sensitive
- In `_read_remote_claim_count`, catch `GitHubError` per repo. Skip that repo, log one line per pass (`remote claims: skipped OWNER/NAME: <error>`), and count the readable repos.
- `_remote_heartbeat` must always write its cache entry once it has a heartbeat, so a failed read cannot make every caller in the pass read again.
Files: 1 sensitive, 1 logic, 2 tests, 1 docs

## Why
Since about 01:05Z on 2026-10-20 every station pass fails at almost every stage. The station log shows the same error 31 to 33 times each for `run_factory`, `assign_queued`, `hand_back`, `publish_lanes`, `close_done_tickets`, `relay_operator`, `post_brain_memory`, `restate_shipped_live` and `post_overdue_standups`:
    station: run_factory failed: GET /repos/<<redacted> repo>/issues?state=open&labels=loom:running,lane:<redacted> -> 404
So for about 4 hours no ticket was claimed, no failed check was handed back, nothing climbed the ladder and the lane status comment stayed at 01:05Z.
The cause is in bus/station.py. `_remote_heartbeat("<redacted>")` calls `_read_remote_claim_count`, which loops over every repo in LOOM_REPOS with no error handling. Two <redacted> repos answer 404 to the station's App token. The exception escapes before `remote-status.json` is written, so the cache is never filled, and every later caller (`_free` lane checks, the lane comment, the beats invariant) reads again and raises again. The failures began when the <redacted> lane's heartbeat came back, which is the first time the claim count was read in this state.
ISSUE-1071 covers the same kind of failure in the standup pass only. This ticket covers the shared cause that now stops the whole pass.

## Summary
- In `_read_remote_claim_count`, catch `GitHubError` per repo. Skip that repo, log one line per pass (`remote claims: skipped OWNER/NAME: <error>`), and count the readable repos.
- `_remote_heartbeat` must always write its cache entry once it has a heartbeat, so a failed read cannot make every caller in the pass read again.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] With one repo in the station's repo list answering 404 to `issues?state=open&labels=loom:running,lane:<redacted>`, `_read_remote_claim_count("<redacted>")` returns the count from the other repos and raises nothing (unit test with a fake GitHub).
- [ ] In the same setup, a full `_free`/lane-availability check and the lane status comment body build without an exception, and the comment shows `Remote claims: <redacted> N/1` (unit test).
- [ ] The skipped repo is logged once per pass as `remote claims: skipped OWNER/NAME: ...`.
- [ ] Live: within one station pass of the deploy, the station log has no `run_factory failed: GET /repos/... lane:<redacted> -> 404` line, and the lane status comment's `Updated` time is less than 10 minutes old.

Size: S

## Out of scope
- Granting the Loom App access to the two repos, or changing which repos LOOM_REPOS lists. Those are operator actions, asked separately.
- The standup pass's own goal-home read (ISSUE-1071).
Part of ISSUE-1052

## Intent
Class: logic
- Lanes with ordered model lists fall back after a per-model quota while pinned tickets retain their requested model.
Files: 1 logic, 1 tests, 1 docs

## Why
On 2026-10-13 the agy lane hit a 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED quota for its one model, gemini-3.8-flash-high, and held the whole lane for 24 hours. The same plan still served claude-opus-5-5-high, claude-sonnet-5-5-high, gpt-oss-120b-medium and gemini-3.8-flash-low (each checked live on 2026-10-14): quotas are per model variant, so a whole subscription sat idle while most of it was available.

## Summary
- A lane may name an ordered model list, `LOOM_<SLOT>_MODELS` (space separated, first is the default), next to `LOOM_<SLOT>_MODEL`.
- When a run fails with a provider limit that names a quota (the runner's existing `[limit]` path), the runner records that model as limited until the reset the provider gave (or the lane's usual hold), and the next pass uses the next model in the list that is not limited. Only when every listed model is limited does the lane hold.
- The heartbeat reason names the model in use and the limited ones, and the PR footer names the model that did the work, as today.
- A ticket's `Model:` line still wins: a ladder model is never swapped for another.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A test with a fake agent that answers the agy quota message for the first model shows the next pass runs the second model and the lane stays available.
- [ ] A test shows the lane holds only when every listed model is limited, with each model's reset in the heartbeat reason.
- [ ] A test shows a ticket with a `Model:` line is never run on a different model from the list.

Size: M

## Out of scope
- Choosing which models to list for each lane (a config change after this merges).
- Provider limits that are not per model (a whole account out of credit).

+MODEL_LIMIT_FILE="$LOOM_HOME/state/usage/$SLOT.models"

+  local model="$1" now saved_model ends
+  now="$(date +%s)"
+  [ -f "$MODEL_LIMIT_FILE" ] || return 1
+  while read -r saved_model ends _; do
+    [ "$saved_model" = "$model" ] && [[ "$ends" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] &&
+      [ "$ends" -gt "$now" ] && { printf '%s' "$ends"; return 0; }
+  done < "$MODEL_LIMIT_FILE"
+  return 1

+  mv "$tmp" "$MODEL_LIMIT_FILE"

+  local models="$1" model ends why="" first=1
+  for model in $models; do

+      [ "$first" -eq 1 ] || why="$why, "

## Intent

- Restore shared family sale trips when floor members' vendor stacks reach the collective slot threshold, while keeping the bag-room hold's per-member lift check.
Files: 2 logic, 1 tests

## Why
The pre-ship review of bridge ship e4d0a545 (2026-10-21) found that ISSUE-1309 made `family_sale_slots` a subset of `family_town_run_needed` (`bag_pressure.py:495`). So the ISSUE-1204 shared-sale trip can no longer fire: that case now waits for `vendor_wait_trip` instead.

Restore the ISSUE-1204 path: a family whose sale slots call for a town run starts the shared sale trip as before ISSUE-1309, without undoing ISSUE-1309's fix.

- [x] ISSUE-1309's case still holds; its tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] Live: the bridge log shows the ISSUE-1204 shared-sale trip line for a family within 48h of the ship that carries this; not built: live bridge verification requires a deployment carrying this change.

Size: S

## Out of scope
Vendor wait timing.

## Intent
Class: logic
- Add a new bridge-side function at the same seam as `chat.py`/`voice.py` (pure builder in, thin IO adapter around it) that takes one shortlisted candidate name and: (1) confirms the candidate is currently online using a fresh `orchestrator_snapshot` row with the same 60s freshness rule as `_fetch_groundi
Files: 3 logic, 1 tests

## Why
The spec in iac ISSUE-3640 calls for giving a shortlisted recruit one real "interview" moment using the repo's existing inner-voice/chat machinery, instead of inventing a new LLM system. The work is to add a bridge-side caller that asks one guild-appropriate question of one shortlisted online candidate and records the exchange, while keeping the deterministic `RecruitVerdictFor` gate as the sole pass/fail decision and never asking the LLM for a numeric verdict.

## Summary
Add a new bridge-side function at the same seam as `chat.py`/`voice.py` (pure builder in, thin IO adapter around it) that takes one shortlisted candidate name and: (1) confirms the candidate is currently online using a fresh `orchestrator_snapshot` row with the same 60s freshness rule as `_fetch_grounding`; (2) asks them one guild-appropriate question via the existing LLM/grounding path; (3) records the question + reply as data the caller returns. If the candidate is offline, skip them and let the caller try the next shortlisted name rather than blocking. Add tests at the rows-in/rows-out seam with a fake LLM/store and no live model call in CI.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] a shortlisted, online candidate can be asked one question and their reply is captured as data the caller returns
- [ ] an offline shortlisted candidate is skipped, not blocked on
- [ ] the LLM is never asked for a numeric verdict; `RecruitVerdictFor` remains the sole pass/fail gate
- [ ] tested with a fake LLM/store, no live model call in CI

Size: M

## Out of scope
- Where the transcript is stored long-term (iac ISSUE-3650)
- The automatic loop that calls this on a schedule (iac ISSUE-3651)
- A harder, LLM-judged accept/reject gate (explicitly deferred as future, riskier work in the iac ISSUE-3640 spec comment)
Rewritten from issue 14.
Part of ISSUE-512

+++ b/interview.py
@@ -0,0 +1,108 @@
+"""One interview exchange with a shortlisted recruit, before the guild invite.
+
+THE PURE HALF OF THE INTERVIEW STEP. Rows in, one plan out. No database, no
+clock, no LLM - the same seam recruit.py keeps, and for the same reason:
+every branch below is a case somebody has to be able to write a test for
+without a realm running.
+
+WHAT THIS MODULE IS NOT ALLOWED TO DECIDE, and the line is worth stating
+because it is easy to cross by accident. It does NOT judge the candidate.
+Who is worth asking is answered by `RecruitVerdictFor` and `RecruitShortlist`
+in game-module's pure layer, against the guild's real holes - and the LLM is
+never asked for a verdict of any kind. The question below is DETERMINISTIC:
+asking the model to write its own interview question would put
+verdict-shaped language one prompt edit away. The model only answers, in
+character, through the existing chat path.
+
+WHAT IT DOES. Takes one shortlisted candidate's grounding and builds the one
+guild-appropriate question to ask them. Whether the candidate is online is
+the CALLER's read - a fresh `orchestrator_snapshot` row under the same 60s
+freshness rule `_fetch_grounding` enforces - and None here is the skip
+signal: the caller tries the next shortlisted name rather than blocking on
+this one.
+
+WHERE THE EXCHANGE GOES. The bridge-side caller runs the question through
+the inner voice and gets back an InterviewExchange: the question plus the
+reply, as data. Where that transcript is stored long-term is a separate
+question from asking it, and it is out of scope here.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from collections.abc import Mapping
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class InterviewPlan:
+    """The one question to ask one shortlisted candidate.
+
+    `reason` IS ALWAYS SET, on a plan like on recruit.py's actions - a pass
+    that asks somebody has to say why this name, the same way a pass that
+    asks nobody says why not.
+    """
+
+    candidate: str
+    question: str
+    reason: str
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class InterviewExchange:
+    """One recorded interview exchange, as data for the caller to keep.
+
+    `question` is the deterministic question this module built; `reply` is
+    what the candidate said back through the inner voice. Nothing here is a
+    judgement of the candidate - `RecruitVerdictFor` stays the sole
+    pass/fail gate.
+    """
+
+    candidate: str
+    question: str
+    reply: str
+    reason: str
+
+
+def build_question(
+    *,
+    name: str,
+    level: int,
+    race_name: str,
+    class_name: str,
+    zone: str,
+) -> str:
+    """The one guild-appropriate interview question, grounded in the candidate.
+
+    DETERMINISTIC ON PURPOSE - see the module docstring. An officer's
+    question: why this guild, and what the candidate brings to it. Grounded
+    in level, race, class and where they were last seen, so the reply comes
+    back about this character and not about guilds in the abstract.
+    """
+    return (
+        f"What brings you to look for a guild, {name}? You're a level {level} "
+        f"{race_name} {class_name}, last seen in {zone} - what are you hoping "
+        "to find here, and what would you bring to it?"
+    )
+
+
+def plan(*, name: str, snapshot: Mapping | None) -> InterviewPlan | None:
+    """The interview question for one shortlisted candidate, or None.
+
+    `snapshot` is the candidate's grounding as the caller resolved it -
+    level, race_name, class_name, zone - or None when the candidate is not
+    online. None is the skip signal: the caller tries the next shortlisted
+    name rather than blocking.
+    """
+    if snapshot is None:
+        return None
+    return InterviewPlan(
+        candidate=name,
+        question=build_question(
+            name=name,
+            level=snapshot["level"],
+            race_name=snapshot["race_name"],
+            class_name=snapshot["class_name"],
+            zone=snapshot["zone"],
+        ),
+        reason="shortlisted and online - asking the one interview question",
+    )
diff --git a/tests/test_interview.py b/tests/test_interview.py
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..18c7202f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/test_interview.py
@@ -0,0 +1,117 @@
+"""One interview exchange with a shortlisted recruit, before the guild invite.
+
+The interview step gives a shortlisted candidate one real "interview" moment
+through the repo's existing inner-voice/chat machinery instead of inventing a
+new LLM system.
+
+WHAT THESE TESTS ARE PROTECTING, because it is not "the question reads
+nicely". It is that the judgement never moves: who is worth asking is
+RecruitVerdictFor's call in game-module's pure layer, and the LLM is never
+asked for a verdict of any kind here. The question is deterministic - asking
+the model to write its own interview question would put verdict-shaped
+language one prompt edit away - and the model only answers it in character.
+
+Rows in, one exchange out: every test below runs against a fake store and a
+fake voice. No live model call, no database.
+"""
+
+import pathlib
+import re
+import unittest
+
+import interview
+
+DOCKERFILE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "Dockerfile"
+
+
+def snapshot(**kw):
+    """A shortlisted candidate's grounding, as the caller resolves it."""
+    base = {
+        "level": 24,
+        "race_name": "Gnome",
+        "class_name": "Mage",
+        "zone": "Stormwind City",
+    }
+    base.update(kw)
+    return base
+
+
+# Verdict-shaped language, which must never appear in the question the
+# model is given. Matched on word boundaries so "bring" does not trip "rank".
+VERDICT_WORDS = re.compile(
+    r"\b(verdict|score|scored|rating|rate|rank|ranked|grade|pass|fail|accepted|"
+    r"rejected|out of 10|/10)\b",
+    re.IGNORECASE,
+)
+
+
+class AnOnlineCandidateIsAskedOneQuestion(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_the_question_names_the_candidate(self):
+        plan = interview.plan(name="Ziblop", snapshot=snapshot())
+        self.assertIsNotNone(plan)
+        self.assertIn("Ziblop", plan.question)
+
+    def test_the_question_is_grounded_in_who_they_are(self):
+        plan = interview.plan(name="Ziblop", snapshot=snapshot())
+        self.assertIn("24", plan.question)
+        self.assertIn("Gnome", plan.question)
+        self.assertIn("Mage", plan.question)
+        self.assertIn("Stormwind City", plan.question)
+
+    def test_the_question_is_guild_appropriate(self):
+        """An officer's question - why this guild, and what they bring - not
+        small talk and not an interrogation."""
+        plan = interview.plan(name="Ziblop", snapshot=snapshot())
+        self.assertIn("guild", plan.question.lower())
+
+    def test_the_question_is_deterministic(self):
+        """The model never writes its own interview question."""
+        first = interview.plan(name="Ziblop", snapshot=snapshot()).question
+        second = interview.plan(name="Ziblop", snapshot=snapshot()).question
+        self.assertEqual(first, second)
+
+    def test_the_exchange_carries_candidate_question_and_reply(self):
+        exchange = interview.InterviewExchange(
+            candidate="Ziblop",
+            question=interview.plan(name="Ziblop", snapshot=snapshot()).question,
+            reply="I want a guild that runs dungeons together.",
+            reason="shortlisted and online",
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(exchange.candidate, "Ziblop")
+        self.assertTrue(exchange.question)
+        self.assertEqual(exchange.reply, "I want a guild that runs dungeons together.")
+
+
+class AnOfflineCandidateIsSkipped(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_no_snapshot_means_no_question(self):
+        """None is the skip signal: the caller tries the next shortlisted
+        name rather than blocking on this one."""
+        self.assertIsNone(interview.plan(name="Ziblop", snapshot=None))
+
+
+class TheModelIsNeverAskedForAVerdict(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_the_question_carries_no_verdict_shaped_language(self):
+        plan = interview.plan(name="Ziblop", snapshot=snapshot())
+        self.assertIsNone(
+            VERDICT_WORDS.search(plan.question),
+            f"verdict-shaped language in the interview question: {plan.question!r}",
+        )
+
+    def test_the_plan_is_data_not_a_judgement(self):
+        """The plan records what to ask, never whether the candidate is
+        worth asking - that stays RecruitVerdictFor's call."""
+        plan = interview.plan(name="Ziblop", snapshot=snapshot())
+        self.assertFalse(hasattr(plan, "verdict"))
+        self.assertFalse(hasattr(plan, "score"))
+
+
+class TheModuleShipsInTheImage(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_interview_py_is_in_the_dockerfile_copy_list(self):
+        """A module the bridge imports must be COPYed into the image or the
+        container crashes on import - the failure mode test_recruit.py guards
+        for recruit.py."""
+        self.assertIn("interview.py", DOCKERFILE.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
label: GOOD

criteria.text: a shortlisted, online candidate can be asked one question and their reply is captured as data the caller returns
an offline shortlisted candidate is skipped, not blocked on
the LLM is never asked for a numeric verdict; `RecruitVerdictFor` remains the sole pass/fail gate
tested with a fake LLM/store, no live model call in CI

body:
## Why

Of 361 lane fix rounds sampled across the factory on 2026-10-13 and 2026-10-14, 111 involved a failed CI check. This repo had no `.loom/validation.conf`, so lanes opened pull requests here without running the Python suites, and CI found the failures one round later.

## Summary

- Adds `.loom/validation.conf`: lanes run `make test` (the webhook, api and scripts suites that `check.python.yml` runs) with the same placeholder AWS settings, before a pull request opens.
- `interpreter: uv`, since every target runs through `uv run`.
- Without a Postgres service or opengrep in the lane sandbox, the store-backed and SAST-engine tests skip there; `CI` is unset, so the Makefile guards that refuse those skips in CI do not fire. CI still runs them all.

Proof, in a fresh clone through the lane runner's own check sandbox (emptied env, empty scratch HOME, so uv fetched every package):

- The check exits 0 in 58s: 2800 webhook, 297 api and 76 scripts tests passed, no tracked file changed.
- Inverting the compare in `services/webhook/hmac_verify.py` makes it exit 2 with 12 failures.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A lane run on this repo runs the check on the base and on its commit, and opens a pull request only after a green check.
- [ ] CI on this pull request still runs the Postgres-backed tests.
- [ ] A change that breaks a webhook, api or scripts test fails the lane check before any pull request opens.

Size: XS

## Out of scope

- The Postgres-backed `pg-test` target and the opengrep rule tests in the lane check.
- The web and image-build checks.

Part of ISSUE-1143

https://claude.ai/code/<redacted>

title: Lanes run the Python suites before opening a pull request

body:
## Intent
Class: logic
- Escalation counts a failed brief only when its last lane-log failure tag is work (untagged counts as work) and names how many were left out as limit or transient.
- A failed pull request create is parked as transient, like a failed push.
Files: 2 logic, 2 tests

## Why
North star 4 counts tickets that "failed twice on the same model". `bus/metrics.py` (`Collector._failed_run`) counts every brief in a slot's `failed/` folder by its Model line, whatever the failure was. On 2026-10-14 it would report 13 such tickets, but only 3 failed twice doing the work: the rest hit a provider limit, the empty API credit, or a push that failed. The runner already tags each failure in the lane log (`failed: [work|limit|transient] reason`, lanes/run_lane.sh `park`), so the number can say what it means. Also, "pr create failed" is parked as `work` although the agent's work was done and pushed (2026-10-14: a missing label failed ten finished runs). Part of ISSUE-30.

## Summary
- `bus/metrics.py`: for each failed brief, read the last `failed: [kind]` line for that ticket name in `logs/<slot>/<ticket>.log`; count it toward Escalation only when the kind is `work`. A failure with no tag line counts as `work` (older runs), and the number's text says how many were left out as limit or transient.
- `lanes/run_lane.sh`: "pr create failed" is parked as `transient`, like "push failed".

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Tests: two `[limit]` failures on one model do not count; two `[work]` failures do; a failure with no tag line counts; the text names the left-out count. Each fails without the change.
- [ ] A runner test asserts a failed PR create parks as `transient`; it fails without the change.
- [ ] Live: the next daily line's Escalation text shows the left-out count, and its number matches a hand count of `[work]` repeats in the lane logs for that day.

Size: S

## Out of scope
The ladder's own rules; other numbers.

---
Loom ticket example.factory-261-r4, lane claude, model claude-sonnet-5-5.
Refs ISSUE-261

## Intent
Class: logic
- Fix rounds merge the default branch before validation and run the agent on the updated tree.
- A red fix-branch check reaches the agent when the default branch passes; only a red default branch check files a base-check incident.
Files: 1 logic, 1 tests

## Why
A fix round's base check runs on the pull request's own head, not on the default branch. When that head is red because it predates a fix on the default branch, the runner reports a factory incident ("base check exited 1 on the unmodified repo") and parks the ticket in `factory_held.json`. The ticket then sits `loom:running` with no lane, and the pull request it should repair is never brought up to date. Nothing moves until a brain notices by hand.
Seen 2026-10-19 between 03:02Z and 03:24Z:
- ISSUE-585 r7 (lane claude): the baseline record in `example.factory-585-r7.validation.jsonl` has revision `60e9f1ca`, the head of PR ISSUE-856. The one failure is `test_a_goal_the_app_reported_minutes_ago_is_held_not_owed`, which ISSUE-859 fixed on main at 20:45Z on 10-18 (merge `29d14cb1`). Main's unittest was green at that time (`1169449b` success). Incident ISSUE-921 was filed, and ISSUE-585 is held.
- game-orchestrator ISSUE-1108 r5: the baseline revision is `69cb60fe`, the head of game-orchestrator PR ISSUE-1126. The game-orchestrator main is at `94881bf6`. Incident ISSUE-923 was filed, and ISSUE-1108 is held.

## Summary
In `lanes/run_lane.sh`, when the run is a fix round on an existing branch, bring the branch up to date with the default branch first (the same update the factory already does for a conflict) and run the baseline check on that merged tree. Then:
- When the default branch itself passes the check but the pull request head does not, the red check is the ticket's work, not a factory incident. Hand it to the agent as the failing check to fix.
- File a factory incident only when the check fails on the default branch's own head.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A fix round whose pull request head fails the check while the default branch passes it files no factory incident and parks nothing in `factory_held.json`. A test covers it.
- [ ] That fix round runs its agent on the branch updated with the default branch, and the failing check reaches the agent's brief.
- [ ] A check that fails on the default branch's own head still files the base-check incident as before. A test covers it.
- [ ] Live: no new base-check incident over 24 hours names a baseline revision that is a pull request head while the default branch's CI is green (validation jsonl `baseline` records against the incidents filed).

Size: M

## Out of scope
Releasing the tickets already held by incidents ISSUE-921 and ISSUE-923. The brain closes those incidents by hand.

## Why

The operator, 2026-10-13: a backlog ticket in the infra repo "don't start this for at least 12 hours from now". Loom had no way to hold a ticket: anything queued could be briefed and claimed at once. The ticket (iac ISSUE-5314) waits without a state label until this lands.

## Summary

- `bus/tickets.py`: a `Not before: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` header (UTC) is parsed and validated like the others, and left out of the brief the lane reads. `not_before()` returns it as epoch seconds.
- `bus/station.py`: a briefed ticket held by a later `Not before:` is not claimed; the station says it is held. A malformed value is refused as an unusable brief.
- `bus/factory.py`: a held briefed ticket never counts as stalled, and its stall clock starts at the hold time.
- `bus/brain.py`: `brief --not-before TIME` writes the line.
- `docs/<redacted>.md`, `docs/LANES.md`: the brain skips held tickets when filling slots, and what the line does.
- Tests: held and past-hold claims, a malformed value, a held ticket not climbing the ladder.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A ticket with a later `Not before:` is not claimed, and one past it is claimed without the line in its brief (tests that fail without the change)
- [ ] A malformed value is refused, and a held ticket never climbs the ladder (tests)
- [ ] Live: iac ISSUE-5314 stays unclaimed until 2026-10-13T17:00:00Z and is claimed after

Size: S

## Out of scope

- Recurring schedules
- Holds on fix briefs

## Why

PR 369 merged with `import sandbox_caps` in three test modules. That import works under `unittest discover -s tests`, which puts `tests/` on the path, but `python -m unittest tests.test_run_lane`, the way a lane reruns one failing module, imports from the repo root and fails with ModuleNotFoundError for all three.

## Summary

- The three modules import `from tests import sandbox_caps`, which loads both ways.
- `tests/test_sandbox_caps.py` imports every module that uses the probes as `tests.<name>` in a subprocess from the repo root. With `tests/test_dashboard.py` restored from main, it fails.
- The lane check still exits 0 in the check sandbox (79s, 53 skipped); on the host the suite skips only the opt-in `LOOM_TEST_OPENCODE2` test.

- [ ] `python3 -B -m unittest tests.test_run_lane tests.test_dashboard tests.test_rewrite_agent` loads all three modules.

- [ ] CI runs the suite with only the opt-in skip.

+import sys
+import unittest

+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
+USERS = sorted(p.stem for p in (ROOT / "tests").glob("test_*.py")

+class SandboxCapsTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_every_module_using_the_probes_also_loads_by_module_name(self):
+        # `python -m unittest tests.test_run_lane`, the way a lane reruns one
+        # failing module, imports from the repo root, not from tests/.
+        self.assertTrue(USERS)

body:
## Intent
Class: sensitive
- Adds GitHub-backed public <redacted> claims, heartbeats, and stale-claim recovery.
- Routes <redacted> tickets without writing them to a local lane inbox and reports claim usage in lane status.
- Opens remote lane pull requests with the standard intent section, class label, ticket reference, and state update.
Files: 1 sensitive, 3 logic, 1 tests, 1 docs

## Why
<redacted> runs only the brain today. The <redacted> account has a weekly free allowance and a large pool of extra tokens that never expire; no lane spends them. <redacted> has no API, CLI or webhook, so a local runner cannot call it. It can run scheduled tasks on its own VM with a shell, git and a GitHub token, and its brain ticks already write to GitHub unattended. The opencode-go-4 slot runs the <redacted> Spark model, but it bills OpenCode Go and is idle on that subscription's weekly limit, not on the <redacted> account.

## Summary
A remote pull lane: a lane whose worker is not the lane machine but an agent that pulls its work from GitHub.
- Config: a remote lane is one config line (name, tier, `public` scope) plus a test, like any lane. The first one is `<redacted>`, easy and medium tiers, public repos only.
- Dispatch: the brain and the station may give a queued ticket `lane:<redacted>`. The station writes no local brief for it. The lane counts as available while it holds fewer than its slot count of claimed tickets and its last claim or heartbeat is fresh.
- Claim: `python3 -m bus.lane claim --lane <redacted>` (or the closest existing shape) returns the oldest queued `lane:<redacted>` ticket with its brief and base, labels it claimed, and records a heartbeat. Nothing claimed for 2 hours, or a claim with no PR after 3 hours, hands the ticket back to the queue with a `[transient]` reason, so a stopped worker never strands work.
- Open: `python3 -m bus.lane pr` opens the PR from a pushed `loom/<n>-<slug>` branch with the standard lane body (intent section, class label, `Refs #N`), and moves the ticket to `loom:pr`. The same command posts fix rounds for review findings on its own PRs.
- Docs: docs/<redacted>.md gains a lane section: the steps a <redacted> scheduled lane task runs each tick (claim, clone, read the brief, change, run the repo's `.loom/validation.conf` check, push, open the PR, journal one line), separate from the brain tick.
- Status and the dashboard list the remote lane, its claims and its last heartbeat like any other lane.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A test adds a remote lane with one config line, gives it a queued public ticket, and shows that no local brief is written and that `claim` returns that ticket once.
- [ ] A test shows that a stale claim goes back to the queue as `[transient]`, and that a <redacted> repo ticket is never given a `public` remote lane.
- [ ] A test shows that `bus.lane pr` opens a PR whose body passes the lane PR body checks and moves the ticket to `loom:pr`.

Size: M

## Out of scope
- Setting up the <redacted> scheduled task itself (the brain does that in the <redacted> app after this merges).
- <redacted> repos on <redacted> (operator decision pending).
- Any change to the opencode-go-4 slot.

+"""GitHub-pulled work for remote lanes."""
+from __future__ import annotations

+from . import change_class, hunt_plan, pr_repair, tickets
+from .github import GitHub, GitHubError, token_from_env
+from .labels import REMOTE_LANES

+CLAIM_RE = re.compile(r"^<!-- loom:remote-claim v1 ([^ ]+) ([0-9]+) ([0-9.]+) -->$")
+CLAIM_AGE = 2 * 3600
+PR_AGE = 3 * 3600

+
+def _names(issue: Dict[str, Any]) -> List[str]:
+    return [str(x.get("name") if isinstance(x, dict) else x)
+            for x in issue.get("labels") or []]
+

+def _comments(gh: GitHub, repo: str, number: int) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
+    return [c for c in gh.paginate("/repos/%s/issues/%d/comments" % (repo, number))
+            if isinstance(c, dict)]
+
+
+def _claims(comments: Sequence[Dict[str, Any]], lane: str) -> List[Tuple[int, float]]:
+    out = []
+    for index, comment in enumerate(comments):
+        match = CLAIM_RE.fullmatch(str(comment.get("body") or "").strip())
+        if match and match.group(1) == lane:
+            try:
+                out.append((index, float(match.group(3))))
+            except ValueError:
+                continue
+    return out
+
+
+def _hand_back(gh: GitHub, repo: str, issue: Dict[str, Any], lane: str,
+               reason: str) -> None:
+    number = int(issue["number"])
+    labels = [x for x in _names(issue) if x not in ("loom:running", "lane:" + lane)]
+    labels.append("loom:queued")
+    gh.rest("PUT", "/repos/%s/issues/%d/labels" % (repo, number), {"labels": labels})
+    gh.rest("POST", "/repos/%s/issues/%d/comments" % (repo, number),
+            {"body": "[transient] %s" % reason})
+
+
+def _pull_for(gh: GitHub, repo: str, branch: str) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
+    """The pull request whose head is the ticket branch, open or closed, or
+    None. One request: GitHub filters by head instead of listing every pull."""
+    owner = repo.split("/", 1)[0]
+    found = gh.paginate("/repos/%s/pulls?state=all&head=%s"
+                        % (repo, quote("%s:%s" % (owner, branch), safe="")))
+    return next((p for p in found if isinstance(p, dict)), None)
+
+
+def _to_pr(gh: GitHub, repo: str, issue: Dict[str, Any], lane: str) -> None:
+    labels = [x for x in _names(issue) if x not in ("loom:running", "loom:queued")]
+    gh.rest("PUT", "/repos/%s/issues/%d/labels" % (repo, int(issue["number"])),
+            {"labels": labels + ["loom:pr"]})
+
+
+def _recover_and_count(gh: GitHub, repos: Sequence[str], lane: str,
+                       now: float) -> int:
+    """Tickets the remote lane holds and still works on. A held ticket whose
+    branch already has a pull request moves to loom:pr; one with no pull
+    request goes back to the queue when its last heartbeat is older than
+    CLAIM_AGE or its first claim older than PR_AGE."""
+    active = 0
+    for repo in repos:
+        found = gh.paginate("/repos/%s/issues?state=open&labels=loom:running,lane:%s"
+                            % (repo, quote(lane, safe="")))
+        for issue in found:
+            if not isinstance(issue, dict) or "pull_request" in issue:
+                continue
+            claims = [at for _, at in _claims(_comments(gh, repo, int(issue["number"])), lane)]
+            if not claims:
+                continue
+            branch = tickets.branch_for(int(issue["number"]), str(issue.get("title") or ""))
+            if _pull_for(gh, repo, branch) is not None:
+                _to_pr(gh, repo, issue, lane)
+                continue
+            if now - max(claims) > CLAIM_AGE or now - min(claims) > PR_AGE:
+                _hand_back(gh, repo, issue, lane,
+                           "remote lane claim expired without a pull request")
+                continue
+            active += 1
+    return active
+
+
+def _candidates(gh: GitHub, repos: Sequence[str], lane: str) -> List[Tuple[str, Dict[str, Any]]]:
+    """(repo, issue) for each public queued ticket assigned to the lane in one
+    of its tiers, oldest first."""
+    found: List[Tuple[str, str, Dict[str, Any]]] = []
+    for repo in repos:
+        if not tickets.REPO_RE.fullmatch(repo):
+            raise ValueError("expected OWNER/NAME, got %r" % repo)
+        info = gh.rest("GET", "/repos/%s" % repo).data
+        if not isinstance(info, dict) or info.get("<redacted>") is not False:
+            continue
+        for item in gh.paginate("/repos/%s/issues?state=open&labels=loom:queued,lane:%s"
+                                % (repo, quote(lane, safe=""))):
+            if _takes(item, lane):
+                found.append((str(item.get("created_at") or ""), repo, item))
+    found.sort(key=lambda row: (row[0], row[1], int(row[2]["number"])))
+    return [(repo, item) for _, repo, item in found]
+
+
+def _takes(item: Any, lane: str) -> bool:
+    if not isinstance(item, dict) or "pull_request" in item:
+        return False
+    names = _names(item)
+    if "loom:queued" not in names or "lane:" + lane not in names:
+        return False
+    try:
+        difficulty = tickets.parse(item.get("body"))[0].get("Difficulty", "")
+    except ValueError:
+        return False
+    return difficulty in REMOTE_LANES[lane]["tiers"]
+
+
+def _take(gh: GitHub, repo: str, issue: Dict[str, Any], lane: str,
+          now: float) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+    number = int(issue["number"])

+    gh.rest("PUT", "/repos/%s/issues/%d/labels" % (repo, number), {"labels": labels})

+
+
+def claim(gh: GitHub, repos: Sequence[str], lane: str = "<redacted>",
+          now: Optional[float] = None) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
+    """Claim the oldest public queued issue assigned to a configured lane."""
+    if lane not in REMOTE_LANES:
+        raise ValueError("unknown remote lane: %s" % lane)
+    now = time.time() if now is None else now
+    if _recover_and_count(gh, repos, lane, now) >= REMOTE_LANES[lane]["slots"]:

+## Remote pull lane
+
+The `<redacted>` lane runs on a remote VM and pulls its ticket from GitHub. It does
+not use the station's local brief inbox. A scheduled lane task runs these
+steps on each tick:
+
+1. Pull the Loom checkout, publish availability with
+   `python3 -m bus.lane heartbeat --lane <redacted>`, then run
+   `python3 -m bus.lane claim --lane <redacted>`.
+   The command returns the oldest eligible public ticket and its rendered
+   brief. If there is no work, end the tick.
+2. Clone that repository, check out the brief's `loom/<n>-<slug>` branch,
+   then read the brief and make its change.
+3. Run the repository's `.loom/validation.conf` check, commit and push the
+   branch. Keep a heartbeat current while working with
+   `python3 -m bus.lane heartbeat OWNER/NAME#N --lane <redacted>`.
+4. Open the pull request with `python3 -m bus.lane pr OWNER/NAME#N
+   --base BASE`. The command writes the standard Intent section, class label
+   and ticket reference, then moves the ticket to `loom:pr`.
+5. Journal one line on the ticket describing the result.
+
+Claims expire after two hours without a heartbeat. A claim without a pull
+request expires after three hours and returns to `loom:queued` with a
+`[transient]` reason. The brain tick remains a separate process and follows
+the regular brain instructions above.
+
 ## Handing off stage work
 
 Every brain may stop short: out of budget, out of time, or out of scope.

+        if path.endswith("/issues/4") and method == "GET":

+        if path.endswith("/issues/4/labels") and method == "PUT":
+            self.issues[4]["labels"] = [{"name": x} for x in body["labels"]]
+        m = re.search(r"/issues/(\d+)/comments$", path)
+        if m and method == "POST":
+            n = int(m.group(1))
+            self.comments.setdefault(n, []).append(
+                {"id": 100 + len(self.comments[n]), "body": body["body"], "created_at": "now"})
+        m = re.search(r"/issues/comments/(\d+)$", path)

+    def paginate(self, path):
+        names = [x["name"] for x in self.issues[4]["labels"]]

+        if "issues?state=open&labels=loom:running" in path:

+        m = re.search(r"/issues/(\d+)/comments$", path)

## Why
The dashboard ticket list shows which model worked on each ticket, but there was no way to filter by it — the operator could not answer "what did model X work on" without scanning every row.

## Summary
- `/tickets` now accepts a `model` query parameter that filters the ticket list to that model

- Models come from the ticket rows and PR footers, the same source already shown on each row

- [ ] Visiting `/tickets?model=<name>` shows only tickets worked on by that model
- [ ] The ticket page renders a chip per model with its ticket count
- [ ] Clicking a model chip filters to that model; "Clear filters" resets
- [ ] Existing state and goal filters keep working alone and combined with the model filter
- [ ] All 47 dashboard tests pass, including the new model-filter test

Size: XS

## Out of scope
- Filtering by lane (only model was asked for)
- Model filter on other dashboard pages (Floor, Backlog)

## Why
The station's `plan-check-failed` invariant was broken when the Grug - Chief check held lane pull request ISSUE-1285 for 37 minutes, reporting that 1 of 9 plan checks failed. The issue asks for a brief that fixes the underlying cause of that failure rather than only documenting the broken invariant.

## Summary
Investigate `bus/hunt_plan.py` and the Grug - Chief evaluation logic to find the failing plan check, correct the root cause (such as an invalid size format, missing acceptance criteria, or incorrect live criterion check), and restore successful PR evaluation.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Identify exactly which of the 9 plan checks fails in `bus/hunt_plan.py` for PR ISSUE-1285
- [x] Fix the root cause in the repository code or check logic
- [ ] Verify live that the Grug - Chief check passes and shows `Grug - Chief: success` without the 37-minute hold; not built: cannot run against live GitHub
- [x] Confirm the `plan-check-failed` invariant no longer triggers for valid briefs

Size: S

## Out of scope
- Modifying PR ISSUE-1285's content or review comments rather than the check mechanism
- Changing lane routing rules or unrelated invariant checks
- Adding new check categories not present in `hunt_plan.py`

body:
## Intent
Class: logic
- Elder, Guard and Smasher now share one public publish seam (personas/review_publish.py) instead of Guard and Smasher importing underscore-<redacted> names from Elder's dispatch module.
- The degrade/publish decision is derived once as PublishOutcome (check conclusion, review event, persona result, Activity-feed degraded reason); no change to published conclusions, results or feed rows.
Files: 8 logic, 9 tests, 2 docs

## Why
`personas/code_reviewer/dispatch.py` is 921 lines and `dispatch_code_review` alone is ~475 of them, mixing payload-unpack, diff-fetch, LLM review, two publish surfaces, capture, structured logging, activity-feed writes, and judge gating. The shared publish machinery is <redacted> to the code_reviewer module while two other personas import it by underscore name today (`personas/guard/dispatch.py:38` and `personas/smasher/dispatch.py:33` import `_publish_shape`, `_resolve_result`, `_build_review_result`, etc.). <redacted> cross-persona imports mean the seam already exists but has no owner, no `__all__`, and no stability contract - a rename inside code_reviewer silently breaks Guard and Smasher. The "did it degrade / did publish fail" decision is re-derived in three places (`_publish_shape`, `_resolve_result`, and the `record_check_verdict` write-site). This is candidate 9 from the 2026-06-08 arch-review note on ISSUE-142, re-verified against the tree on 2026-07-05, sibling of the TokenedGitHubClient extraction (ISSUE-510).

## Summary
- Promote the cross-persona fetch/publish helpers out of `personas/code_reviewer/dispatch.py` into a public shared seam (e.g. `services/_shared/personas/_review_publish.py` or similar), with public names and an explicit `__all__`;
- Update Guard and Smasher imports to use the new public names;
- Extract a typed `PublishOutcome` (publish state x verdict) produced once and threaded to both `_resolve_result` and `record_check_verdict`, so the degrade/publish decision has one derivation.
- Keep the detector modules (sast/sca/secret/iac) where they are - ADR-0012's ownership-by-import decision stands for detectors; this issue only moves the publish/orchestration seam that is ALREADY consumed by 3 personas (rule-of-three met).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] No persona imports an underscore-<redacted> name from another persona's module (grep-clean for `from personas.code_reviewer.dispatch import _`)
- [ ] `PublishOutcome` (or equivalent) is the single derivation of the degrade/publish decision, consumed by both the check-run resolve path and the activity-feed write path
- [ ] Behavior-preserving: both service suites green with no test-expectation changes on publish semantics ("no lies" contract intact)
- [ ] `dispatch_code_review` measurably smaller; orchestration steps unit-testable without mocking httpx at depth

Size: M

## Out of scope
- TokenizedGitHubClient transport unification (ISSUE-510)
- Generalizing the async job runner (deferred to 4th async persona, see above)
- Moving detector modules
- Per-persona async enqueue/run machinery stays duplicated until a FOURTH async persona lands (today: Elder, Guard, Smasher are async; Warder and Pulse are inline)
Rewritten from issue 511.

+(a check run and an inline review) and all fetch the PR diff the same way.
+This module is the one owner of that shared machinery, so no persona imports
+an underscore-<redacted> name from another persona's module:
+
+  * the GitHub reads every review needs (`fetch_pr_diff`, `fetch_file_contents`,
+    `prior_finding_keys`);
+  * the degradation vocabulary (`is_real_degradation` and friends);
+  * `PublishOutcome`, the SINGLE derivation of "did it degrade / did a publish
+    surface fail" - the check conclusion, the review event, the persona result
+    string and the Activity-feed degraded reason all read off one value, so
+    the check run, the log and the feed cannot tell different stories ("no
+    lies", ADR-0003).
+
+Rendering of the Elder-voiced review body stays in `code_reviewer.dispatch`.

+    "PersonaResultStr",
+    "PublishOutcome",
+    "ReviewMode",
+    "fetch_file_contents",
+    "fetch_pr_diff",
+    "fetch_pr_diff_with_scope",
+    "is_blackout",
+    "is_low_confidence",
+    "is_partial_coverage",
+    "is_real_degradation",
+    "plan_publish",
+    "prior_finding_keys",
+]
+
+log = logging.getLogger(f"{os.getenv('DD_SERVICE', 'grug')}.persona.code_reviewer")
+
+# 10s (was 30s) - a GitHub diff fetch is fast; the over-generous 30s let a
+# hung fetch alone eat most of the webhook Lambda budget (ISSUE-252). Well under
+# the 60s budget. NOTE: the FULL synchronous path (diff + review LLM + publish
+# + dedup + capture + judge, xretries x2 backends) is NOT bounded by 60s - a
+# hung backend can blow it; the real fix is async offload (ISSUE-272).
+DIFF_FETCH_TIMEOUT = 10
+# The dedup comments-fetch is on the SYNCHRONOUS webhook path (now a 60s
+# Lambda budget, ISSUE-252) and is best-effort: it must not be able to exhaust the
+# budget before its own try/except degrades to post-everything. So it
+# gets a tight per-request timeout + a low page cap - distinct from the
+# 10s diff fetch. 3 pages x 100 = 300 comments covers virtually every
+# PR; beyond that, dedup degrades to partial (a few duplicate comments -
+# the safe direction) rather than risking a hard handler timeout.
+_COMMENT_FETCH_TIMEOUT = 4
+_MAX_COMMENT_PAGES = 3
+
+# Literal (not bool) so a future "degraded"/"experimental" mode can't
+# silently invert `if not blocking` call sites.
+ReviewMode = Literal["advisory", "blocking"]
+
+# Closed set so a new return site can't introduce an undocumented value.
+# `review_rejected` (ISSUE-770): the check-run landed but GitHub returned a
+# deterministic 4xx on the inline review. A completed pass minus its
+# advisory surface - the durable lane treats it as terminal, never redrives.
+PersonaResultStr = Literal[
+    "pass", "fail", "skipped", "publish_failed", "review_rejected",
+    "unhandled_error",
+]
+
+# Degradations that are NOT a failure to review. `no_diff` means there was
+# nothing to look at (an empty commit, a docs-only push already covered) - the
+# rest of dispatch already treats it as equivalent to clean at the two publish
+# gates, and treating it as an alarm here contradicted that.
+#
+# Observed live on ISSUE-801: an empty re-trigger commit produced "Grug eyes cloudy
+# this pass - read for self", which reads as "the reviewer broke" for a PR
+# where simply nothing had changed.
+BENIGN_DEGRADATIONS = frozenset({"no_diff"})

+

+# degradation, where it saw nothing: the findings it DID publish are valid,
+# diff-anchored evidence, so the surfaces must not tell the author to

+# clean result, not a trusted one: findings from the rest still publish, the
+# check stays advisory, and the surfaces say low confidence rather than
+# "could not see".

+
+# Degradations whose findings are real, diff-anchored evidence and publish.
+PUBLISHABLE_DEGRADATIONS = frozenset({PARTIAL_COVERAGE, LOW_CONFIDENCE})
+
+
+def is_real_degradation(reason: str | None) -> bool:
+    return bool(reason) and reason not in BENIGN_DEGRADATIONS
+
+
+def is_partial_coverage(reason: str | None) -> bool:
+    """Elder saw most of the diff, not none of it."""
+    return reason == PARTIAL_COVERAGE
+
+
+def is_low_confidence(reason: str | None) -> bool:
+    """Elder has an answer, but a short empty one nobody confirmed."""
+    return reason == LOW_CONFIDENCE
+
+
+def is_blackout(reason: str | None) -> bool:
+    """Elder produced nothing usable this pass - the 'could not see' case.
+
+    Split out from `is_real_degradation` so partial coverage stops borrowing
+    the blackout vocabulary. Both are still 'news' for `worth_an_email`; they
+    are simply not the same news."""
+    return is_real_degradation(reason) and reason not in PUBLISHABLE_DEGRADATIONS

## Intent
Class: sensitive
- Escalation now climbs a green, reviewed pull request when its ticket has a pending brain fix.
Files: 1 sensitive, 1 tests

## Why
`bus.brain escalate` refuses a repeatedly stuck ticket whose pull request is green and reviewed with no open thread ("nothing to fix ... land it instead"), even when a brain fix (`<!-- loom:brain-fix v1 -->`) is pending on the ticket. `bus.brain merge` refuses the same pull request because that fix is pending. When no lane picks the fix up, neither command moves the ticket. `_nothing_to_fix` in bus/brain.py checks checks, the review check, threads and conflicts, but never `_pending_brain_fix`.
Seen on 2026-10-22 at 03:52Z: issue 1211 of another repo (PR ISSUE-1269), brain fix posted 2026-10-21 06:56Z naming an unmet criterion and no lane run since (21 hours); a ticket in a <redacted> repo, brain fix posted 2026-10-21 23:40Z, ticket briefed 4 times with no claim. Both escalate calls answered "has nothing to fix ... land it instead", and merge on ISSUE-1269 answered "a brain fix is pending on the ticket".

## Summary
- In `_nothing_to_fix` (or in `escalate` before calling it), treat a pending brain fix on the ticket as something to fix, so the ticket climbs the ladder and the fix goes to the next rung's lane.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Unit test: a ticket with a green, reviewed pull request and a pending brain-fix comment is escalated to its next rung, not refused.
- [x] Unit test: the same ticket with no pending brain fix is still refused with "nothing to fix".
- [x] Existing escalate tests pass.
- [ ] Live: the next `bus.brain escalate` on a ticket with a pending brain fix and a green pull request prints a `rung N` line, read from the brain's tick output; not built: live execution is outside this code change.

Size: S

## Out of scope
- Why a lane does not claim a briefed fix round.
Part of ISSUE-1449

## Why
Tracks ISSUE-802 item 1. When a crafter's spellbook cannot be read (`_fetch_standin_known` in bridge.py answers None on a database error), `standin.walled` correctly does not judge the craft and returns "". But `standin.sits_out` reads that "" as "the craft can move" and returns "", so `standin.step` treats the member as one who should sit out. If the family has no stand-in row yet, one database blip writes a fresh sit-out row, and the crafter can then sit out a whole run while its craft is in fact walled.

## Summary
In standin.py, make an unread spellbook never create a new sit-out row:
- In `sits_out`, after the trade and goal checks and before `walled`, when `facts.known is None`: if `facts.current` is None (no row yet), return a reason such as "<name>'s spellbook was not read this pass, so no new sit-out row is written"; if a row already exists, leave it as it stands (return "" so `step` keeps it, exactly as today).
- Keep every other behavior of `sits_out` and `step` the same.
- Add tests in tests/ (follow the existing standin tests): with `known=None` and no current row, `step` writes no row and the reason names the unread spellbook; with `known=None` and an existing row, the row stands; with a known spellbook the behavior is unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] With the spellbook unread and no current row, no sit-out row is written, and the reason says the spellbook was not read (test that fails without the fix)
- [ ] With the spellbook unread and a row already in place, the row stands unchanged (test)
- [ ] The full suite `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'` passes on Python 3.12

Size: S

## Out of scope
- The other items of ISSUE-802
- How the spellbook is read (`_fetch_standin_known`)

## Intent
Class: logic
- A weapon or armour drop the loot council gives nobody in the family is now voted Disenchant by a roster member whose live Enchanting can take it apart, and Pass by everybody else, so the materials land in the Enchanter's bags; before, every member greeded it and the winner vendored it.

Both fixes are already merged. In th
Files: 4 logic, 2 tests, 1 docs

The family needs an Enchanter so rare drops can be disenchanted instead of vendored. <redacted> (mage) is already assigned tailoring + enchanting (`197,333`), and `orchestrator_roster.professions` confirms it, but `OPEN_ORDER` opens trades sequentially: tailoring is first, enchanting is sixth. body:
## Why
The operator read the station's Discord posts on a phone on 2026-10-12 and asked: "Change these to be what loom goal it is, then expandable to see more info within". Today each two-hourly report is one long wall of text whose first line is the goal home's full title, followed by a GitHub link that unfurls into a large preview card; seven goals make the channel unreadable. The same message also showed two relay gaps: the operator attached a screenshot, but the operator note carried only the text ("change these"), so the brain could not see what was meant; and the station's "Noted" acknowledgement unfurled another large GitHub card.

## Summary
- Reports (`forward_reports`): post one short message per report, through the bot when its token is set (else the webhook as today): a bold short goal name (from the goal home title, or a `Short name:` line in the goal home body when present) and the report's first line. Then create a thread on that message (`POST /channels/{id}/messages/{message id}/threads`, named after the goal and time) and post the full report and the comment link inside it, so tapping the message expands it. With only the webhook, fall back to today's single message.
- Every station post suppresses link previews (the message flag for suppressed embeds), so no GitHub card unfurls.
- Operator notes (`relay_operator`): append each attachment's URL (images and files) to the note under an "Attachments:" line, so the brain can open them; a message with only an attachment is relayed too.
- The acknowledgement says only "Noted for the brain" with the note's link (no preview), and names the goal only when the operator named one.
- Tests with the existing fakes: a report becomes a short message plus a thread holding the full text; previews are suppressed on every post; attachments reach the note; an attachment-only message is relayed; the webhook-only fallback still sends one message.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A report is posted as a short message with the goal's short name and a thread holding the full report, with previews suppressed (tests that fail without the change)
- [ ] An operator message with a screenshot produces a note that links the screenshot, and an attachment-only message is relayed (tests)
- [ ] Live: the next round of reports in the channel reads as one short line per goal, each expanding to the full report

Size: M

## Out of scope
- The report's content (the brain writes it)
- Slash commands

+    def _report_by_bot(self, token: str, issue: Dict[str, Any],
+                       comment: Dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
+        """One short line in the channel, then a thread on it holding the full
+        report and the comment link, so tapping the line expands it."""
+        chan = self.s.channel_id
+        name = self._short_name(issue)
+        body = self._report_body(comment)
+        first = next((line.lstrip("#").strip() for line in body.splitlines()
+                      if line.lstrip("#").strip()), "")
+        line = ("**%s** %s" % (name, first)).strip()
+        if len(line) > SHORT_LINE_MAX:
+            line = line[:SHORT_LINE_MAX - 4].rstrip() + " ..."
+        ok, made = self._bot(token, "POST", "/channels/%s/messages" % chan, {
+            "content": line, "allowed_mentions": {"parse": []}})
+        if not ok:
+            return False
+        # The line is out: from here a failure is logged and not retried, so
+        # the line is never posted twice.
+        msg_id = str(made.get("id") or "") if isinstance(made, dict) else ""
+        where = self._report_thread(token, msg_id, name) if msg_id.isdigit() else ""

+            # lost behind a line that does not expand.

+        for part in self._chunks(body + ("\n" + link if link else "")):
+            ok, _ = self._bot(token, "POST", "/channels/%s/messages" % where, {

+    def _report_thread(self, token: str, msg_id: str, name: str) -> str:

+                                   "auto_archive_duration": THREAD_ARCHIVE_MINUTES})

+        return thread_id if ok and thread_id.isdigit() else ""

## Intent
Class: logic
- Rule 8 flags a local action after a working-tree branch switch; scratch output: ::error::.github/workflows/scratch.yml:10: Rule 8.
- Rule 11 flags conflicting version labels for one pinned action SHA; scratch output: ::error::Rule 11.
- Rule 12 flags a gh command in an arc-pool job; scratch output: ::error::.github/workflows/scratch.yml:9: Rule 12.
- Rules 3, 4, and 10 are declared skipped and named in the clean-run summary.
- Parity fixture directories for rules 8, 11, and 12 record canonical verdicts with violating cases; the test suite checks those verdicts.
- Scratch commit fbd9259 exited 1 with three violations; the normal linter run exited 0.
Files: 24 logic, 1 tests

## Why
This repo publishes the reusable workflows the rest of the fleet consumes, but its workflow-hygiene gate is five rules behind the canonical linter in example/infra. Rules 8, 11, and 12 are in scope and currently absent, allowing future violations to pass the gate in the repo that defines shared CI for the fleet. 

## Summary
Port rules 8, 11, and 12 from the canonical linter in example/infra. Add explicit skip declarations for rules 3, 4, and 10 (already in scope but correctly inert because this repo has no manifest or Ansible tree). Create parity fixtures under .github/scripts/fixtures/ for each newly implemented rule, following the existing rule5_parity convention, and wire them into the test suite. Ensure the runtime output names the skipped rules as the canonical linter does.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `for r in 8 11 12; do grep -qE "Rule $r\b" .github/scripts/workflow_hygiene.py || echo "rule $r missing"; done` prints nothing
- [ ] For each of rules 3, 4, 10 a grep returns a line and runtime names them as skipped
- [ ] Each new rule has a parity fixture dir under .github/scripts/fixtures/ and tests pass with non-zero expected-violation counts
- [ ] `python3 .github/scripts/workflow_hygiene.py` exits 0 reporting clean
- [ ] A scratch commit adding one bad shape per rule makes the linter exit non-zero naming that rule, and the output is recorded on the pull request 

Size: M

## Out of scope
- De-duplicating the two linter copies into one shared module
- Implementing rules 3 and 4 as real checks (declared skips only)
- Fixing any live rule violations in sibling repos
Rewritten from issue 119.

+#
+# The bridge answers it with a chain of five gates (town errand, gear, stuck

+GATE_GEAR = "gear"
+GATE_BAG_STUCK = "bag-hold-stuck"
+GATE_BAG_FULL = "bags-near-full"
+GATE_TOWN_FIRST = "town-first"
+
+GEAR_EMPTY_SLOTS = 6
+GEAR_MIN_PURSE = 20000
+
+

+    """The family may be sent in."""
+
+

+    """The family waits, and `gate` is the gate that said so."""

+

+    name -> pieces waiting in the post, `free_slots` is name -> free bag slots.
+    `gear_since` and `town_since` are the monotonic times those holds began
+    (None: not holding), `stall` the seconds the family's queue head has gone
+    without a run, `hold` the previous bag hold reading, `armed` whether any
+    member already carries this dungeon's job.
+    """

+    gear: dict | None = None
+    mailed: dict | None = None
+    gear_since: float | None = None
+    free_slots: dict | None = None
+    hold: object = None
+    armed: bool = False
+    town_since: float | None = None
+    stall: float = 0.0
+
+
+def _held(since: float | None, now: float, stall: float) -> float:
+    """How long a hold has stood: its own clock, or the queue's stall if longer."""
+    return max(now - (now if since is None else since), stall)
+
+

+    if facts.errand_active:
+        return Withhold(GATE_ERRAND, "the family is on its town errand (ISSUE-365)")
+    return None
+
+
+def _gear_gaps(facts: Facts) -> list:
+    """The funded members with a gear gap worth holding for."""
+    mailed = facts.mailed or {}
+    short = []

+    return short
+

+    short = _gear_gaps(facts)

+        bag_pressure.CAMPAIGN_RESUME_CEILING_SECONDS

+    return Withhold(GATE_GEAR, "gear-up first: " + ", ".join(short))

+DRESSED = {"equipped": ["mainhand"] + ["s%d" % i for i in range(16)], "purse": 50000}

+

## Intent
Class: logic
- A persistent safe-mode marker prevents OpenWrt boot startup and watchdog re-arming until the operator clears it.
- The OpenWrt deploy now installs and verifies the init service alongside the agent package.
Files: 3 logic, 2 tests, 1 docs

## Why
Pathbond installs the default route on the device it runs on, and when a tunnel cannot carry traffic the device loses all connectivity including its admin path, with no watchdog or route-revert to recover. A real OpenWrt deploy path and safer route handling are needed so a bad config cannot lock the operator out.

## Summary
Add a watchdog that removes pathbond's default route and restores underlying WAN routes when no path is reachable for N seconds, never install a default route through a tunnel with no completed handshake, give direct-fallback routes an explicit metric so they cannot outrank netifd's routes, add a real OpenWrt deploy path that syncs the whole package and verifies it matches the repo, and consider a boot delay or safe-mode flag so a bad config cannot lock the operator out at START=95.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Watchdog removes pathbond's default route and restores underlying WAN routes when no path is reachable for N seconds
- [ ] No default route is installed through a tunnel with no completed handshake
- [ ] Direct-fallback routes carry an explicit metric so they cannot outrank netifd's routes
- [ ] A real OpenWrt deploy path syncs the whole package and verifies it matches the repo
- [ ] A boot delay or safe-mode flag prevents a bad config locking the operator out at START=95

Size: L

## Out of scope
The bonding policy itself, which already works correctly with weighted ECMP.
Rewritten from issue 130.

## Why
The operator asked for the README to show Loom's factory workflow, nice and simple. The old README described an earlier layout (a local dispatcher, goals in a local folder) and none of the brain, station, review or verify loop that runs today. It also spelled out the review bot's handle in a public file. Part of ISSUE-30.

## Summary
- One diagram of the loop: goal, brain, ticket, station, lane, pull request, review bot and CI (findings back to the lane), merge, ship, verify, back to the brain.
- Eight short steps, the label conveyor, a who-does-what table, the lane list, layout, how to run it and the rules.
- Parts not merged yet are marked as being built (ISSUE-94 hand-back and ready label, ISSUE-84 phone report).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] README renders the diagram on GitHub and is ASCII only (hygiene test passes)
- [ ] Every part it describes as running exists on main, and unmerged parts are marked as being built
- [ ] No handle of the review bot appears in the file

Size: XS

## Out of scope
- docs/ rewrites

Multi-project by design: one loom, many goals. +A software factory that drives goals forward on every AI subscription you +have. You write a goal. Loom turns it into tickets, builds them in parallel, +reviews and fixes them, ships them, proves they worked live, and keeps going +until the goal is done. + +## The factory + +```mermaid +flowchart LR + G[Goal
home issue] --> B[Brain

Why, What, 3 checks] + T --> S[Station

proof line + metric moved] + V --> B +``` + +1. **Goal.** One issue in the project's repo, labelled `loom:goal`. It says + what done looks like, how progress is measured, and the project's ship + rules. +2. **Brain.** Every tick it measures the goal, puts regressions first, ranks + the open problems by the goal's own measure, and writes tickets for the + top ones, enough to keep every lane busy. +3. **Ticket.** An issue with Why, What, exactly three acceptance checks + (one names a test that fails without the fix, one is the live proof), + Size and Out of scope. +4. **Station.** Runs once a minute on the lane machine. Findings and + failed checks go back to the lane that wrote it, which fixes them on the + same pull request and answers each thread. Clean pull requests are + marked ready. +7. **Merge, ship, verify.** The brain merges ready pull requests, ships them + under the project's rules, and closes a ticket only when its proof shows + up live and the metric it targets moved. +8. **Journal and report.** Each tick leaves a journal on the goal; every two + hours a short report goes to the operator's phone.
