body:
## Why
The operator wants every agent transcript readable from the phone. The Loom dashboard on the cluster will store transcripts in Postgres and serve them over the tailnet (example/infra, its own ticket). The lane machine is where transcripts are made: API lanes archive them under `$LOOM_HOME/logs/<slot>/<ticket>/` (claude JSONL under `.claude/projects`, opencode's `opencode.db`), every lane writes `$LOOM_HOME/logs/<slot>/<ticket>.log`, and the brain tick's claude sessions land in the operator's claude projects folder for `$LOOM_HOME/brain`. `lanes/viewer/serve.py` already knows how to read these formats.

## Summary
- `bus/transcripts.py`: turn one finished run into the upload body `{ticket, slot, model, outcome, started_at, finished_at, events: [{ts, role, kind, text}]}`; kind is `text`, `tool_use`, `tool_result` or `log`. Reuse the viewer's readers (move shared parsing into a module both import, so there is one parser). Scrub every text with the station's `scrub` (local paths) and a token pattern filter (GitHub, Anthropic, OpenAI, AWS, Cloudflare key shapes become `[redacted]`); cap each event at 20,000 characters and the body at 8 MB, dropping the oldest tool results first.
- `bus/station.py`: a pass `upload_transcripts` that, for each brief in a slot's `done/` or `failed/` not yet uploaded (a ledger in the station state, like the reports ledger), builds the body and POSTs it to `LOOM_TRANSCRIPT_URL` with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, the token read from SSM `LOOM_TRANSCRIPT_TOKEN_SSM` with the same reader as the webhook. It never logs the token or the URL's query, retries on the next pass, and gives up on one run after 5 failures with one station log line. With either setting empty the pass does nothing. Brain ticks upload too, as `brain/<UTC timestamp>`, from the newest session files after each tick (`lanes/mac/brain.sh` writes the session's start time into `state/brain.json`).
- `lanes/mac/install.sh`: pass `LOOM_TRANSCRIPT_URL` and `LOOM_TRANSCRIPT_TOKEN_SSM` to the station. The URL and the SSM path come from the installing environment, never this repo.
- Tests with fakes: a finished claude-JSONL run and an opencode run become the right events; secrets and local paths are scrubbed; limits hold; upload happens once and is retried after a failure; nothing is sent without the settings.
- docs/LANES.md: a paragraph on uploads, replacing the localhost viewer as the way to read transcripts (the viewer stays for local use).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A finished run uploads once with scrubbed, capped events, and a failure is retried (tests that fail without the change)
- [ ] Claude JSONL, opencode and plain log runs all convert to events through the one shared parser (tests)
- [ ] Live: after install with the two settings, the next finished ticket's transcript appears on the dashboard

Size: L

## Out of scope
- The dashboard and database (example/infra)
- Uploading transcripts of runs that finished before this ships

+"""One finished run as the body the station uploads to the dashboard.
+
+    {ticket, slot, model, outcome, started_at, finished_at,
+     events: [{ts, role, kind, text}]}
+
+kind is text, tool_use, tool_result or log; role is user, assistant,
+thinking, tool or runner. The events come from the one transcript parser
+(bus/sessions.py, which the viewer reads too): the CLI's own session record,
+then the lane log of the run's last attempt. Every text is scrubbed of local
+paths and credential shapes, each event is capped at EVENT_MAX characters, and
+the body at BODY_MAX bytes, dropping the oldest tool results first.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+import re
+import time
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional
+
+from . import sessions
+from . import text as _text
+
+EVENT_MAX = 20000
+BODY_MAX = 8 * 1024 * 1024
+CUT = "\n[cut]"
+REDACTED = "[redacted]"
+# Redaction patterns for provider key shapes (none of them is a secret).
+TOKENS = [
+    # GitHub: classic, OAuth, app, refresh and fine-grained tokens.
+    re.compile(r"\b(?:gh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{36,}|github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{22,})"),
+    # Anthropic, then OpenAI (sk-, sk-proj-, sk-svcacct-, sk-admin-).
+    re.compile(r"\bsk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}"),
+    re.compile(r"\bsk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}"),
+    # AWS: an access key id, and a 40-character base64 secret key (with a
+    # digit, an upper and a lower case letter, so no word or git sha matches).
+    re.compile(r"\b(?:AKIA|ASIA)[A-Z0-9]{16}\b"),
+    re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z0-9+/])(?=[A-Za-z0-9+/]{0,39}[0-9])(?=[A-Za-z0-9+/]{0,39}[A-Z])"
+               r"(?=[A-Za-z0-9+/]{0,39}[a-z])[A-Za-z0-9+/]{40}(?![A-Za-z0-9+/=])"),
+    # Cloudflare: a 40-character API token of the same mix, and a 37-character
+    # hex global API key.
+    re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z0-9_-])(?=[A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,39}[0-9])(?=[A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,39}[A-Z])"
+               r"(?=[A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,39}[a-z])[A-Za-z0-9_-]{40}(?![A-Za-z0-9_-])"),
+    re.compile(r"\b[0-9a-f]{37}\b"),
+    # Any bearer token.
+    re.compile(r"(?i)\bbearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9._~+/=-]{8,}"),
+]
+# A home directory as Claude Code names a project after it (-Users-name-...).
+MANGLED_HOME_RE = re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z0-9_.-])-(?:Users|home)-[A-Za-z0-9._-]+")
+# The runner's line that starts an attempt (lanes/run_lane.sh).
+START_RE = re.compile(r"^\[(\d{4}-\d\d-\d\dT\d\d:\d\d:\d\dZ)\] \S+ start, lane ", re.M)
+ROLES = {"user": "user", "assistant": "assistant", "thinking": "thinking"}
+
+
+def scrub(text: str) -> str:
+    """The text without local paths or credential shapes."""
+    text = MANGLED_HOME_RE.sub("<path>", _text.scrub_paths(text))
+    for pattern in TOKENS:
+        text = pattern.sub(REDACTED, text)
+    return text
+
+
+def _cap(text: str, tail: bool = False) -> str:
+    """At most EVENT_MAX characters: the head, or for a log the tail (where
+    the outcome is)."""
+    if len(text) <= EVENT_MAX:
+        return text
+    keep = EVENT_MAX - len(CUT)
+    return CUT.lstrip("\n") + "\n" + text[-keep:] if tail else text[:keep] + CUT
+
+
+def _input_text(tool: str, inp: Any) -> str:
+    """A tool call as text: its name, then each input as key: value."""
+    if not isinstance(inp, dict):
+        return "%s: %s" % (tool, inp if isinstance(inp, str) else json.dumps(inp))
+    lines = [tool]
+    for key, value in inp.items():
+        lines.append("%s: %s" % (key, value if isinstance(value, str) else json.dumps(value)))
+    return "\n".join(lines)
+
+
+def _event(ts: Optional[str], role: str, kind: str, text: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+    return {"ts": ts, "role": role, "kind": kind,
+            "text": _cap(scrub(text), tail=kind == "log")}
+
+
+def convert(events: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
+    """Parser events (bus/sessions.py) as upload events: a tool call becomes
+    a tool_use and, when it has output, a tool_result."""
+    out = []
+    for e in events:
+        kind, ts = e.get("kind"), e.get("ts")
+        if kind in ROLES:
+            out.append(_event(ts, ROLES[kind], "text", str(e.get("text") or "")))
+        elif kind == "tool":
+            tool = str(e.get("tool") or "?")
+            out.append(_event(ts, "assistant", "tool_use", _input_text(tool, e.get("input") or {})))
+            if e.get("output"):
+                out.append(_event(ts, "tool", "tool_result", str(e["output"])))
+        elif kind == "log":
+            out.append(_event(ts, "runner", "log", str(e.get("text") or "")))
+    return out
+
+
+def _size(value: Any) -> int:
+    return len(json.dumps(value).encode("utf-8"))
+
+
+def limit(body: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+    """The body at most BODY_MAX bytes as JSON: the oldest tool results go
+    first, then, if it is still too big, the oldest events of any kind."""
+    events = body["events"]
+    total = _size(dict(body, events=[])) + sum(_size(e) + 1 for e in events)
+    if total <= BODY_MAX:
+        return body
+    keep = [True] * len(events)
+    order = ([i for i, e in enumerate(events) if e["kind"] == "tool_result"]
+             + [i for i, e in enumerate(events) if e["kind"] != "tool_result"])
+    for i in order:
+        if total <= BODY_MAX:
+            break
+        keep[i] = False
+        total -= _size(events[i]) + 1
+    return dict(body, events=[e for e, k in zip(events, keep) if k])
+
+
+def _utc(at: float) -> str:
+    return time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime(at))
+
+
+def run_body(home: Path, slot: str, ticket: str, outcome: str, model: str,
+             claude_projects: Path, codex_sessions: Path) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+    """A lane run (briefs/<slot>/done|failed/<ticket>.md) as an upload body.
+    Raises ValueError for an unsafe slot or ticket name."""
+    events = sessions.session_events(slot, ticket, home, claude_projects, codex_sessions)
+    log = home / "logs" / slot / ("%s.log" % ticket)
+    started, finished = None, None
+    for e in sessions.log_events(log):
+        # The log holds every attempt on this slot; this run is the last.
+        starts = list(START_RE.finditer(e["text"]))
+        if starts:
+            started = starts[-1].group(1)
+            e = dict(e, text=e["text"][starts[-1].start():])
+        events.append(e)
+        finished = _utc(log.stat().st_mtime)
+    return limit({"ticket": ticket, "slot": slot, "model": model, "outcome": outcome,
+                  "started_at": started, "finished_at": finished, "events": convert(events)})
+

body:
## Intent
Class: sensitive
- Station decision refusals and rewrite outcomes are recorded in a redacted daily JSONL event log with seven days of retention.
- Repeated same-reason failures without a matching success trigger a deduplicated factory invariant after 60 minutes and appear in standups and the dashboard floor health card.
Files: 2 sensitive, 2 logic, 2 tests

## Why
On 2026-10-17 three factory stalls were found only by reading the station log by hand. The unproven limit refused every claim for hours. The triage rewriter skipped every <redacted> repo ("no agent command for this repo") and failed on public ones for days. Eleven tickets pinned to a model logged "waits: no free lane takes model" every pass. Each one repeated the same line hundreds of times and never reached Discord, the dashboard, or an invariant. The factory must catch its own failures; a log line is not an alarm.

## Summary
- The station writes one JSON line per decision it refuses or fails, to `$LOOM_HOME/logs/events.jsonl`: time, kind (for example `rewrite_failed`, `rewrite_skipped`, `model_wait`, `not_claiming`), item `OWNER/NAME#N` when there is one, lane, model and reason. Rotate it daily and keep 7 days.
- An invariant (beside the existing `gate_held`) fires when one kind with the same reason repeats for 60 minutes with no success of that kind in the same window. It goes in the standup's "not going well" line and files one factory ticket, deduplicated by kind and reason, as the existing invariants do.
- The dashboard's health view lists the open repeated-failure invariants.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A test: 60 minutes of `rewrite_skipped` with one reason and no successful rewrite opens one invariant and one ticket, and a second hour does not file a second ticket. The test fails on main.
- [ ] A test: a kind that also had a success in the window opens nothing.
- [ ] Live: within a day of the deploy, events.jsonl exists with lines of at least three kinds, and any open repeated-failure invariant appears in the next standup.

Size: M

## Out of scope
- Moving the event log into Postgres (decision 0002 may take it later).
- Changing what the station decides; this only records and surfaces it.

## Intent
Class: logic
- The overworld dialogue box now has a 3px ink border around a 2px white rule, replacing the copper-rimmed ticket frame.
- Dialogue text is inset 3px inside the white rule (8px from the box edge) and wraps to that width.
- A dialogue box slides up from below the screen over 8 frames with ease-out when a conversation opens; a top box slides down from above.
- Consecutive lines of one conversation (including a reply right after a yes/no) appear in place without sliding again.
- Battle messages appear in place in the HUD and never slide.
- A TextBox can set its own typing speed (slow, mid, fast) over the player's text-speed option; an unknown speed throws.
- The down-triangle continue arrow appears only once the page has fully typed (unchanged behavior, now exposed as TextBox.typed()).
Files: 2 logic, 1 tests

## Why
The issue requests implementing authentic Pokemon-style dialogue boxes with proper borders, text padding, character-by-character text display, arrow indicators, and smooth open/close animations to enhance the game's visual presentation and player experience.

## Summary
Create a DialogueBox component/class that renders with a 3px black border and 2px white inner border, displays text character by character with a configurable speed, shows a triangle arrow indicator when text is complete, applies 2-3 pixel padding from edges, and includes a slide-up animation when opening.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] DialogueBox component renders with black border (3px) and white interior (2px)
- [ ] Text displays character by character with smooth animation and configurable speed
- [ ] Triangle arrow indicator appears when text completes and 'A to continue' prompt is shown
- [ ] Dialogue box has proper padding (2-3 pixels from edges) with correct text alignment
- [ ] Slide-up animation plays on open with smooth easing

Size: M

## Out of scope

- Sound effects during dialogue

body:
## Why
The operator's north-star goal (in this repo's goal home) is done only when nine numbers hold for 7 days in a row, and it asks for "a daily line with each of the 9 numbers against its target, and the projected date all 9 hold for 7 days". The first line was computed by hand on 2026-10-13 (comment on ISSUE-30). Nothing measures the numbers on its own, so the streak cannot be counted.

## Summary
- `bus/metrics.py` computes, over the last 24 hours across `LOOM_REPOS`:
  1. Flow: lane pull requests open over 6 hours; median hours from `loom:briefed` to `loom:merged` per merged ticket; tickets left past the last rung for over 24 hours (a "tried every rung" comment with no later `<!-- loom:rung 0 -->`).
  2. Throughput: merged pull requests per goal-home repo; merged tickets and how many are `loom:verified`.
  3. Spread: lane runs per lane from `briefs/*/done` and `failed`, the Anthropic share, and slot use (the share of station passes, from the lane heartbeats, where a free slot sat idle while a ticket was queued for its lane).
  4. Escalation: tickets that failed twice on the same `Model:`.
  5. Quality: regressions shipped and still unfixed after 2 hours (`loom:urgent` tickets open over 2 hours after a regression note), merges whose head lacked the review check, and fix pull requests without a new or changed test file.
  6. Autonomy: `needs-operator` asks opened.
  7. Visibility: each goal home's newest report age.
  8. Self-repair: factory faults ("past the last rung", parked runs) without a linked ticket.
  9. Generic: files in this repo naming the WoW terms the hygiene test lists.
- The station posts the line once a day after `LOOM_DIGEST_HOUR` as a `<!-- loom:metrics v1 -->` comment on the Loom goal home (`LOOM_METRICS_GOAL`, owner/name#N), each number against its target with a pass or fail mark. It keeps a streak count (consecutive days with all nine passing) and the projected date the streak reaches 7, and sends one Discord line with the pass count and streak.
- Tests with the existing fakes for each number, the pass marks, the streak and the once-a-day posting.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `bus/metrics.py` computes all nine numbers with pass or fail against their targets (tests that fail without the change)
- [ ] The station posts the daily line once a day with the streak and projected date, plus one Discord line (tests)
- [ ] Live: the next day's line appears on the goal home and matches a hand count of at least two of its numbers

Size: L

## Out of scope
- Changing the targets
- A dashboard page
Part of ISSUE-30

+"""Daily measurements of Loom's nine factory outcomes."""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import os
+import re
+import statistics
+import subprocess
+import sys
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from datetime import datetime, timedelta
+from typing import Any, Dict, Iterator, List, Sequence
+
+from .github import GitHub
+from .labels import LANES
+
+MARKER = "<!-- loom:metrics v1 -->"
+REPORT = "<!-- loom:report v1 -->"
+WINDOW = 86400
+TEST_FILE = re.compile(r"(^|/)(test_[^/]+\.py|[^/]+_test\.[^/]+|[^/]+\.(test|spec)\.[^/]+)$")
+FIX = re.compile(r"<!-- loom:fix|\bfix(?:es|ed)?\b", re.I)
+REGRESSION = re.compile(r"\bregression\b", re.I)
+GENERIC_TERMS = re.compile(r"\b(wow|warcraft|guild|raid|realm|dungeon|playerbot)\b", re.I)
+REPAIR_REF = re.compile(r"\b(?:Refs|Fixes) ([A-Za-z0-9._-]+/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+)#(\d+)")
+
+
+def stamp(value: Any) -> float:
+    if isinstance(value, (int, float)) and not isinstance(value, bool):
+        return float(value)
+    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
+        return 0.0
+    try:
+        return datetime.fromisoformat(value.replace("Z", "+00:00")).timestamp()
+    except ValueError:
+        return 0.0
+
+
+def names(item: Dict[str, Any]) -> set[str]:
+    return {str(label.get("name")) for label in item.get("labels", [])
+            if isinstance(label, dict)}
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Number:
+    name: str
+    value: str
+    target: str
+    passed: bool
+
+    def line(self) -> str:
+        return "%s %s: %s (target %s)" % (
+            "PASS" if self.passed else "FAIL", self.name, self.value, self.target)
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Totals:
+    pull_old: int = 0
+    past_rung: int = 0
+    merged_tickets: int = 0
+    verified: int = 0
+    asks: int = 0
+    regressions: int = 0
+    unchecked: int = 0
+    fix_no_test: int = 0
+    faults: int = 0
+    goals: int = 0
+    merge_times: List[float] = field(default_factory=list)
+    merged_by_repo: Dict[str, int] = field(default_factory=dict)
+    report_ages: Dict[str, float] = field(default_factory=dict)
+    goal_repos: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
+
+
+class Collector:
+    def __init__(self, gh: GitHub, repos: Sequence[str], home: str,
+                 now: float, review_check: str, trusted: Sequence[str] = ()) -> None:
+        self.gh, self.repos, self.home = gh, list(repos), home
+        self.now, self.since, self.review_check = now, now - WINDOW, review_check
+        self.trusted = {login.lower() for login in trusted}
+        self.events: Dict[tuple[str, int], List[Dict[str, Any]]] = {}
+        self.comments: Dict[tuple[str, int], List[Dict[str, Any]]] = {}
+
+    def list(self, path: str) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
+        return [item for item in self.gh.paginate(path) if isinstance(item, dict)]
+
+    def issue_events(self, repo: str, number: int) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
+        key = (repo, number)
+        if key not in self.events:
+            self.events[key] = self.list("/repos/%s/issues/%d/events" % key)
+        return self.events[key]
+
+    def issue_comments(self, repo: str, number: int) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
+        key = (repo, number)
+        if key not in self.comments:
+            self.comments[key] = self.list("/repos/%s/issues/%d/comments" % key)
+        return self.comments[key]
+
+    def trusted_comment(self, comment: Dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
+        return not self.trusted or str((comment.get("user") or {}).get("login") or "").lower() in self.trusted
+
+    def label_time(self, repo: str, issue: Dict[str, Any], label: str) -> float:
+        found = [stamp(e.get("created_at")) for e in self.issue_events(repo, int(issue["number"]))
+                 if e.get("event") == "labeled"
+                 and (e.get("label") or {}).get("name") == label]
+        return max(found, default=0.0)
+
+    def passes(self, repo: str, sha: str) -> bool:
+        # rest() returns a Response or raises GitHubError, never None; only
+        # .data can be None (an empty or non-JSON body), hence the dict check.
+        # A GitHubError is left to propagate on purpose: counting a failed
+        # lookup as "no review check" would fail the Quality number on an API
+        # blip. Station._post_metrics_comment catches it and retries the pass.
+        data = self.gh.rest("GET", "/repos/%s/commits/%s/check-runs" % (repo, sha)).data
+        checks = data.get("check_runs", []) if isinstance(data, dict) else []
+        return any(c.get("name") == self.review_check for c in checks)
+
+    def _finished(self, lane: str, kind: str) -> Iterator[str]:
+        """Paths of the briefs a lane finished in the window under done/ or failed/."""
+        try:
+            entries = os.scandir(os.path.join(self.home, "briefs", lane, kind))
+        except FileNotFoundError:
+            return
+        with entries:
+            for entry in entries:
+                if (entry.name.endswith(".md") and entry.is_file()
+                        and self.since <= self._completed(entry) <= self.now):
+                    yield entry.path
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _completed(entry: os.DirEntry) -> float:
+        info = entry.stat()
+        return max(info.st_mtime, info.st_ctime)
+
+    def local_runs(self) -> tuple[Dict[str, int], Dict[str, Dict[str, int]], int]:
+        counts: Dict[str, int] = {lane: 0 for lane in LANES}
+        failures: Dict[str, Dict[str, int]] = {}
+        unlinked = 0
+        for lane in LANES:
+            for kind in ("done", "failed"):
+                for path in self._finished(lane, kind):
+                    counts[lane] += 1
+                    if kind == "failed":
+                        unlinked += self._failed_run(path, failures)
+        return counts, failures, unlinked
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _failed_run(path: str, failures: Dict[str, Dict[str, int]]) -> int:
+        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
+            body = fh.read()
+        issue = re.search(r"^Issue: (\S+#\d+)$", body, re.M)

+        self.pulls = [self.pr]
+        self.comments = {1: [{"body": metrics.REPORT + "\nReport",
+                              "created_at": iso(NOW - 1000),
+                              "user": {"login": "trusted-bot"}}], 2: []}
+        self.events = {2: [{"event": "labeled", "label": label("loom:briefed"),
+                            "created_at": iso(NOW - 8000)},

+        self.checks = [{"name": "Review"}]
+        self.files = [{"filename": "tests/test_feature.py", "status": "modified"}]
+        self.posts = []
+
+    def paginate(self, path):
+        if path.endswith("/issues?state=all&per_page=100"):
+            return self.issues
+        if path.endswith("/pulls?state=all&per_page=100"):
+            return self.pulls
+        if "/issues/" in path and path.endswith("/comments"):
+            return self.comments[int(path.rsplit("/", 2)[1])]

## Why

The operator-approved soaks on <redacted> (2026-10-13, traces on ISSUE-5306) measured the contained vLLM coder:

- Two streams: the hottest zone reached 79.7 C, and the thermal guard paused the box after 21 minutes (3-minute mean 75.6 C). No power cut.
- One stream: 30 minutes, 70.7 C peak, 65.5 C mean, 69 tok/s, the guard never paused.

The coder should therefore serve one stream. With that settled, the gateway route can be turned on: it only answers requests that name the coder's model, one at a time, and the guard takes it out of routing while the box is hot.

## Summary

- `roles/vllm_coder/defaults/main.yml`: `vllm_coder_max_num_seqs` from 2 to 1, with the measurements as the reason.
- `<redacted>/deployment.yaml`: `<redacted>_VLLM_ENABLED` set to true (it already carries `<redacted>_VLLM_GUARD_URL`).
- `test_contained_vllm.py`: the manifest may turn the route on only with the guard URL set, one parallel request, and one sequence in the role.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The role runs one sequence and the gateway turns the route on only behind the guard (role and gateway tests pass)
- [ ] After the playbook and the sync, `vllm-coder` runs with `--max-num-seqs 1` and the gateway lists the `<redacted>-vllm` target on its dashboard
- [ ] A chat completion through the gateway naming the coder's model is answered by the vLLM target

Size: XS

## Out of scope

- The assay agentic-coding run (next on ISSUE-5306)
- A Loom lane on the Sparks

Refs ISSUE-5306

https://claude.ai/code/<redacted>

## Intent
Class: logic
- Add a lane validation contract that runs the pull request server test command and records absent lint, format, and type checks.
Files: 1 logic, 1 tests

## Why
Lanes need the repository's checks before opening pull requests.

## Summary

## Why
Since 2026-10-17 the Spark lanes come first in every tier, hard included. A Spark run can end with nothing to show because the model ends its turn on an announcement instead of a tool call. issue 44 of another repo on spark-3 (2026-10-18 02:29-03:19Z, Nemotron 3.5 Super VL through opencode) made 14 tool calls in 50 minutes. One of them was a `find /` that ran into the 120 s shell timeout. The run's last line was "Let me check the `.loom` directory and look at the route probe test patterns..." with no tool call after it. opencode took the text-only turn as the end of the session, and the station recorded "[work] agent made no commit and wrote no reason". The factory climbed the ticket to gpt-6-sol on codex-2, which is right, but the Spark's 50 minutes produced nothing, and the model never got to the work.

## Summary
- In the lane runner, when an opencode session ends with no commit and no `.loom/summary.md` reason, and its last assistant turn had no tool call, continue the same session once with "Continue: carry out the step you just described, then commit or write .loom/summary.md". Only then report the run failed.
- Tell Spark lanes in the brief not to search the whole filesystem (`find /`), and to read the repository's build files instead.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A test with a fake opencode whose first session ends on a text-only turn shows the runner continuing it once and then succeeding; it fails on main.
- [ ] A test: a session that ends on a text-only turn twice is reported failed after exactly one continue, with the reason "ended on a described step without taking it".
- [ ] Live: over 48 hours after deploy, Spark runs that fail with "no commit and wrote no reason" fall by at least half.
Size: S

Size: S

## Out of scope
- Changing which tiers the Sparks serve.
- The model ladder.
Part of ISSUE-703

title: A Spark run that ends on a described step gets one continue before it fails

body:
## Why
Refs ISSUE-874. characters.online reads 0 for guild members who are in the world: any account-mate's logout clears the flag for the whole account, and it stays clear until the member's next save, up to 15 minutes (measured 2026-10-12: all 142 Cave and <redacted> members in the world in 36 samples over 9 minutes, 2 to 7 of them reading online 0 each time). ISSUE-388 and ISSUE-718 moved guild runs and the API pages to the fresh snapshot, but guild work still reads the flag. In 3 hours the bridge logged 150 `guild gear: X waits for gear: it is offline`, 10 `guild jobs: X is offline`, 3 dues and 2 corps skips, so members in the world got no job step for minutes at a time.

## Summary
- Replace every `characters.online` presence read with a fresh-snapshot read: in bridge.py `_JOB_MEMBERS_SQL` (keep its snapshot join and derive `online` from it), `_DUES_MEMBERS_SQL`, `_CORPS_MEMBERS_SQL`, `_GUILD_POST_SQL` (both halves of the UNION) and `_STANDING_SQL`; in apiv2/raidteams.py, apiv2/search.py, apiv2/social.py (both queries) and map_server.py's character read, use apiv2/presence.py `of()` or the same LEFT JOIN on orchestrator_snapshot with updated_at inside presence.FRESH_SECONDS.
- One shared SQL fragment or helper for the join, so the window is defined once.
- Each guild jobs pass logs `guild jobs: <guild>: <n> of <m> members in the world` once.
- New tests/test_presence_reads.py scans the SQL string constants in bridge.py, apiv2/*.py and map_server.py and fails on any selected `<alias>.online` column from characters (apiv2/presence.py's offline flag read is the only allowed exception).
- A guild jobs test: a member row with a fresh snapshot gets its gear step even when the old flag column would have read 0.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] tests/test_presence_reads.py passes, and fails without the change (11 current sites)
- [ ] The full suite `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'` passes
- [ ] Live proof after the bridge ship: `guild jobs: Cave: 71 of 71 members in the world` (and <redacted>) appears while the snapshot holds all members, and `waits for gear: it is offline` drops from 150 per 3 hours to 0 for members with a fresh snapshot

Size: M

## Out of scope
- The core's account-wide offline write (game-module ticket)
- Any change to job selection other than who counts as online

+"""Presence-facing SQL must derive online state from the fresh snapshot."""
+
+import ast
+import pathlib
+import re
+import sys
+import types
+import unittest
+from unittest import mock
+
+sys.modules.setdefault("pymysql", types.ModuleType("pymysql"))
+
+from apiv2 import presence  # noqa: E402
+import guildjobs  # noqa: E402
+
+ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+FILES = [
+    ROOT / "bridge.py",
+    *sorted((ROOT / "apiv2").glob("*.py")),
+    ROOT / "map_server.py",
+]
+
+
+def sql_literals(path):
+    tree = ast.parse(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+    for node in ast.walk(tree):
+        if isinstance(node, ast.Constant) and isinstance(node.value, str):
+            value = node.value
+            if re.search(r"\b(?:SELECT|FROM|JOIN)\b", value, re.I):
+                yield value
+
+
+class TestPresenceReads(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_character_online_columns_are_not_selected(self):
+        for path in FILES:
+            with self.subTest(path=path.name):
+                for sql in sql_literals(path):
+                    self.assertNotRegex(sql, r"\b[a-z][a-z0-9_]*\.online\b")
+
+    def test_shared_join_defines_the_snapshot_window(self):
+        join = presence.snapshot_join("c", "p")
+        self.assertIn("p.name = c.name", join)
+        self.assertIn(f"INTERVAL {presence.FRESH_SECONDS} SECOND", join)
+        self.assertIn(
+            "(s.name IS NOT NULL) AS online", (ROOT / "bridge.py").read_text()
+        )
+
+    def test_guild_jobs_snapshot_member_is_eligible_for_gear(self):
+        source = (ROOT / "bridge.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+        sql = source[
+            source.index("_JOB_MEMBERS_SQL = (") : source.index("_JOB_SKILLS_SQL = (")
+        ]
+        self.assertIn("(s.name IS NOT NULL) AS online", sql)
+        self.assertIn('v2_presence.snapshot_join("c", "s")', sql)
+        # Every job decision, including gear, consumes the projected snapshot
+        # value on the member row.
+        gear_candidates = (ROOT / "guildjobs.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+        body = gear_candidates[gear_candidates.index("def gear_candidates(") :]
+        body = body[: body.index("\ndef ", 1)]
+        self.assertIn("if m.online", body)
+        self.assertIn("guildjobs.gear_candidates(members, recent)", source)
+
+        # This models the SQL result row: the snapshot projection says online
+        # even when the saved characters.online value would be zero.
+        member = guildjobs.Member(
+            name="Member",
+            guild="Guild",
+            role=guildjobs.MAINTENANCE,
+            online=True,
+            map_id=0,
+            x=1.0,
+            y=1.0,
+        )
+        step = types.SimpleNamespace(said="buys gear")
+        with mock.patch.object(guildjobs, "gear_step", return_value=(step, "")) as gear:
+            selected = guildjobs.gear_candidates([member], [])
+            self.assertEqual(selected, [member])
+            result = guildjobs._gear_first(member, ({}, []), [], 500)
+        gear.assert_called_once()
+        self.assertIs(result[0], step)
+
+
+def _bridge_function(name):
+    tree = ast.parse((ROOT / "bridge.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+    node = next(
+        n for n in tree.body if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef) and n.name == name
+    )
+    ns = {}
+    module = ast.Module(body=[node], type_ignores=[])
+    exec(compile(module, "bridge.py", "exec"), ns)  # noqa: S102 - bridge.py's own source
+    return ns[name]
+
+
+class TestWorldCounts(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_fresh_snapshot_members_count_in_the_world(self):
+        world_counts = _bridge_function("_world_counts")
+
+        def member(name, guild, online):
+            return guildjobs.Member(
+                name=name,
+                guild=guild,
+                role=guildjobs.MAINTENANCE,
+                online=online,
+                map_id=0,
+                x=1.0,
+                y=1.0,
+            )
+
+        members = [
+            member("Fresh", "Cave", True),
+            member("Stale", "Cave", False),
+            member("Other", "<redacted>", True),
+        ]
+        self.assertEqual(world_counts(members), {"Cave": [1, 2], "<redacted>": [1, 1]})
+        self.assertIn(
+            "sorted(_world_counts(members).items())",
+            (ROOT / "bridge.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8"),
+        )

body:
## Why
Loom assumes the default branch is the trunk. One onboarded repo is a fork whose default branch tracks its upstream, while all of its work merges into a long-lived side branch; lanes started from the default branch, where the files a ticket names do not exist, and five tickets failed on every rung with "agent made no commit" (2026-10-13). Trunk-based work needs one trunk per repo, and a fork cannot always make its trunk the default branch. Part of ISSUE-30.

## Summary
- A goal home may carry a `Trunk: <branch>` line near the top of its body. When present, `bus.brain brief` uses it as the base when `--base` is not given, the lane runner checks out from it, the factory compares PRs against it, and the review and merge code read it as the target.
- `bus.brain status` flags a repo whose last 10 merged PRs mostly target a branch that is neither the default branch nor the goal home's Trunk ("work merges into X; set Trunk: X on the goal home").
- `bus.brain onboard` writes no Trunk line by default, and docs/BRAIN.md explains when to add one.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Tests: a brief under a goal with `Trunk: side` gets base `side`; an explicit `--base` still wins; status flags a repo whose recent merges target an undeclared branch. Each fails without the change.
- [ ] No behavior changes for a goal home without a Trunk line (existing tests pass unchanged).
- [ ] Live: after the goal home of that fork gets its Trunk line, the next ticket there opens its PR against the side branch.

Size: M

## Out of scope
Changing any repository's default branch; syncing a fork with its upstream.

---
Loom ticket example.factory-230-r3, lane claude, model claude-sonnet-5-5.
Refs ISSUE-230
